sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793

items.q: Chronic kidney disease in this chapter is defined histologically by more than what percentage of interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy or glomerular sclerosis?
items.exp: CKD: >5% of interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy/glomerular sclerosis, with a decrease in the number of functional nephrons. (Book p793)

items.q: Fill up: CKD is characterised by a ______ in the number of functional nephrons.
items.exp: CKD definition: >5% interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy/glomerular sclerosis with ↓ number of functional nephrons. (Book p793)

items.q: Match each pathology with its associated condition in the causes table — 1) Vascular  2) Glomerular (diabetes)  3) Tubulo-interstitial fibrosis … A) Diabetic nephropathy  B) CTID  C) Ischemic nephropathy
items.exp: Causes table: vascular (RAS, TMA) → ischemic nephropathy; glomerular (diabetes) → diabetic nephropathy; tubulo-interstitial fibrosis (–) → CTID. (Book p793)

items.q: A patient has renal artery stenosis and biopsy shows ischaemic nephropathy. In the causes table, this belongs to which pathology group?
items.exp: Vascular pathology (RAS, TMA) leads to ischemic nephropathy, and together with the glomerular group it produces secondary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis. (Book p793)

items.q: Which glomerular diseases are grouped together with IgA nephropathy to cause chronic glomerulonephritis (CGN)?
opts: RAS and TMA, producing ischaemic nephropathy
Diabetes mellitus and hypertension, causing diabetic nephropathy
Sarcoidosis and Sjögren's syndrome, causing interstitial infiltration
items.exp: Glomerular row of the causes table: IgA/MPGN/FSGS/membranous nephropathy → CGN (chronic glomerulonephritis). (Book p793)

items.q: Match each cause of CKD with its label in the table — 1) IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous nephropathy  2) Diabetes  3) RAS/TMA … A) Diabetic nephropathy  B) Ischemic nephropathy  C) CGN (chronic glomerulonephritis)
items.exp: Table mapping: IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous → CGN; diabetes → diabetic nephropathy; RAS/TMA → ischaemic nephropathy; primary tubulointerstitial fibrosis → CTID. (Book p793)

items.q: In the causes table, vascular and glomerular pathology together are grouped as producing secondary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis.
opts: False — only vascular disease produces tubulointerstitial fibrosis
False — the grouping is labelled primary fibrosis
True, but only when diabetes is absent
items.exp: The brace in the table labels the vascular and glomerular rows as 'secondary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis', leaving primary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis as CTID. (Book p793)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed as conditions associated with CKD in the causes table. Which is the odd one out?
opts: IgA nephropathy, MPGN, FSGS and membranous nephropathy
items.exp: The associated conditions listed are RAS/TMA, IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous nephropathy and diabetes; PSGN is a self-limited disease not listed here. (Book p793)
